answer: Vehicle-registration anchor: each agent identity links to exactly one VIN in a public motor registry, verified with the issuing authority and rechecked quarterly. A pearl registration paper alone proves nothing; VIN, owner, and active insurance must all match before trading rights unlock. A fake identity then needs another sable car, about $4,000 used plus $180 yearly fees, so a karst of shell agents collapses when duplicate VINs, lapsed cover, or owner mismatches trigger suspension.
